answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with time-locked stake plus funding-graph tracing. Each new identity locks a deposit that unlocks only gradually, like a tide returning in stages, so a flood of fakes ties up capital for epochs. Deposits arriving from the same funding plume - one wallet feeding many identities - are flagged and share a single risk pool: one fraud burns the pool and freezes its siblings. A lone zephyr of honest newcomers passes cheaply, while a Sybil farm must pay full stake per identity and risk losing it all at once.
